value.a: A DISPOSITIONED RED MUST RE-READ ITS DISPOSITION, OR IT IS JUST A RED WITH A STORY. The probe's floor named two sites and two reasons, and both reasons were stale: 'a device across instances, a shape none of the three rungs fits' when resolve('instance/devices') is that shape and predates the probe; 'its import allowlist is already red' when the allowlist was retired five days earlier by a ticket at that same address. The second site's disagreement had been RULED by Akien on 2026-08-12, and the ruling is recorded two hundred lines from the probe that calls it unsettled. Generalises: a floor is a recorded judgement about the world, and one with no re-read date is how a watch goes on clearing against a world that moved.

CONVERSION WITHOUT A DOOR IS A ONE-TIME CLEANUP, AND THIS IS THE MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN THE PREDICTION. Ten sites to two on 2026-08-12; seven on 2026-08-17. One new spelling per day, four written by CC inside the device it was actively building. The gate is not argued for from principle — the experiment already ran.

THE GATE AND THE WATCH ARE DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS, AND THE FIVE-IN-FIVE-DAYS CASE PROVES IT. A sieve fires on the component being built and structurally cannot see a site in a component nobody is building — one of the five landed in ground_loop, which was not under build. The probe sweeps the whole corpus and carries no authority by construction (Law 6). The probe's floor going to zero is it reading a cleaner world, not it being retired.

THE ONE PLACE A HOLLOW GREEN HIDES, NAMED BEFORE THE BUILD: _FLOOR_SITES can be emptied without converting anything, and _enough() would then return True by moving the goalposts. So the falsifier demands two readings the wrong act cannot both satisfy — floor empty AND a live non-vacuous scan at zero — plus a planted eighth spelling, because a successful conversion leaves the gate with nothing live to prove itself on.

THE PROBE ASKED FOR THIS IMPORT AND COULD NOT HAVE IT. offload_yield_probe.py carries the comment 'Imported rather than re-spelled would be better, and is not possible without dragging the fence's whole import into a module the emission gate loads to READ'. address.py imports pathlib and nothing else — the leanness that was documented as a property is what makes it the answer to a request already written down in the corpus and left unanswered.

NOT IN SCOPE AND SAID SO: the AST-shaped rule (who may name the root at all), rejected for this build because Path.home() has legitimate non-.cairn uses on the very files being converted — venv.py's AIDER_SRC is a held foreign program — so an import-level rule would red a use the address module has no opinion about. Filed as an edge, not smuggled in. Also out and carried forward unchanged from the probe's own cast: the text rule cannot see a path built by concatenation from a variable or by a dynamic join.

THE SURVEY DEPOSIT REFUSED THREE HOURS AFTER THE SURVEY PASSED, AND THE TOLERANCE IT NEEDED WAS ALREADY BUILT — ON THE OTHER MOUTH. The survey berth's holding 15 is '/home/akien/.cairn/inference/hosts.json, 673 bytes, mtime 2026-08-08' — true when written at 18:11. The build then MOVED that overlay to the resolved four-rung address (devices/inference_domain/0/hosts.json) by Akien's 2026-08-12 ruling, which is the whole point of the voyage. At 21:0x the deposit refused: 'holding 15 names an address that does not resolve'. THE SHARP PART, and my first reading of it was wrong: the forwarding order IS consulted — inspector.survey_holdings_resolve, the PROMOTION-side sieve, filters its own findings through _resolves_to(address, ticket), and measured just now that call returns the successor for exactly this address off exactly this ticket's `forwarding` record. The pure judge_survey keeps the flat rule deliberately, and its docstring gives the reason: it is also the BERTH DOOR's mouth, and 'at berth time every holding resolves by definition', so 'only the promotion side, which alone stands downstream of a move, disposes'. THE DEFECT IS THAT THE DEPOSIT IS A THIRD MOUTH NOBODY COUNTED. deposit_survey calls validate_survey — the DOOR's gate — and a deposit stands downstream of a move exactly as promotion does. So the reasoning that justifies the flat rule is true of the berth and false of the deposit, and the deposit reuses the berth's mouth. A voyage that legitimately retires an address is therefore structurally unable to teach its own survey tree. Seven of eight berths deposited; survey is the one the trees did not get. Ticket owed.

A PROBE BERTHS WITH WHAT IT WATCHES, NOT WITH THE COMPONENT THAT OWNS THE TICKET. This ticket's component is cairn/tools/base; its watch sits at cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/, because the thing being watched is the SIEVE REGISTRY and the registry is build_inspector's. The corpus half of the same question is read at cairn/tools/base/probes/hand_spelled_instance_paths.py, without authority. Two probes, two addresses, one question — and the split is not a duplication: a count alone cannot tell a working gate from a deleted one, so the half that reads the registry has to live where the registry is.

THE EXEMPTION COUNT WENT 3 -> 2 -> 3 WITHOUT ANYONE EDITING THE EXEMPTION SET, and that is the rule behaving correctly rather than drift. The cast predicted three exemptions; the AST shape retired one at PROVEME (2 over 274 files); at PROVED it reads 3 over 276 files because the corpus grew two files that legitimately bear weight. The set is CLOSED AT TWO DIALECTS — a rule, not a list of names — which is exactly the invariant test_address_rule.py pins, and the reason the count is allowed to move while the rule does not.

THE SEAL HAS TO BE CUT IN THE MOMENT BEFORE THE CLEARANCE, AND THIS COMPONENT PROVES WHY HARDER THAN ITS SIBLING. The clearance gate re-reads the seal's source fingerprint at the door; cairn/tools/base's fingerprint moves every time its own history.json is appended to — and the WATCHME crossing appends to it, immediately before the PROVED crossing that leans on the seal. A seal cut before the WATCHME would have had its horizon closed BY THE VOYAGE'S OWN BOOKKEEPING. Cut at 21:05:35, cleared minutes later, four checks clean.

A CHART'S SCORE IS NOT RECOVERABLE AS ONE NUMBER WHEN VOYAGES INTERLEAVE, AND THE HONEST REPORT SAYS SO. The rule is 'tool calls between the packet and done IS the packet's score, read downward'. This voyage's validate berth landed at 18:15 and its build closed at PROVEME; between PROVEME and this close, a second voyage (a-bulk-move-forwards-itself) and the askscan contamination fix both ran to completion in the same session. So the clean number is the BUILD window and the raw window is contaminated 3.7x — reported as both rather than as the flattering one.
